name: Gnomeregan
summary: In Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan lies ruined and quarantined after a desperate defense against troggs. Once the greatest technological wonder of the gnomish race, it was their underground capital. Its surviving people live as refugees in nearby Ironforge, while irradiated halls hold mutated troggs, deranged leper gnomes, and rogue mechanical sentries.

sections.title: A Marvel of Iron and Steam
sections.body: Gnomeregan once gathered gnomish invention, competitive craft, and politics beneath Dun Morogh. With help from the nearby dwarves of Ironforge, its people built a vast mechanical complex powered by grinding engines and whirring gears. An intricate ventilation network needed fifteen technicians working around the clock to keep fresh air moving. At Tinkers' Court, gnomes debated and competed as their capital grew into a marvel of industry. During the Second War, they sent the Alliance of Lordaeron siege engines, flying machines, and armaments.

sections.title: The Trogg Invasion and the Poisoning
sections.body: During the Third War, as the Scourge tore through Lordaeron, dwarven excavations at the ancient titan vault of Uldaman awakened primitive troggs beneath Dun Morogh. The creatures burrowed into Gnomeregan's lower foundations, and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque led his forces in a desperate defense. When the city's defenses began to fail, Mekkatorque followed the counsel of his chief advisor, Mekgineer Thermaplugg. He ordered the radioactive waste tanks vented into the lower levels to eradicate the invaders. The toxic gas spread beyond control, and nearly eighty percent of the gnomish population died within days.

sections.title: The Mad Mekgineer's Treason
sections.body: Mekgineer Thermaplugg had secretly coveted High Tinker Mekkatorque's office, and rumors say he knew of the trogg invasion before it began and helped set the disaster in motion. No one verified those rumors, though Mekkatorque believes they could be true. Whatever Thermaplugg intended, events escaped his control. Radiation failed to kill the troggs and drove them into a violent frenzy, while Thermaplugg was trapped in the contaminated lower tiers. Radioactive sickness twisted him into an insane leper gnome. From his throne in Tinkers' Court, he crowned himself techno-overlord of Gnomeregan and commands mindless leper survivors and erratic machinery.

sections.title: A Fragile Victory
sections.body: From Tinkertown in Ironforge, High Tinker Mekkatorque coordinates the effort to reclaim Gnomeregan and sends Alliance adventurers into its toxic depths to break Thermaplugg's rule. Slaying the Mekgineer at the heart of Tinkers' Court ends his command over the rogue defenses and leper cohorts, bringing long-sought vengeance for his monumental betrayal. Yet a permanent reconquest remains elusive. Irradiated sludge, mutated beasts, and troggs still choke the deeper tunnels. Mekkatorque is assembling gyrodrillmatic excavationators and broader military plans to reclaim his people's ancestral home.

faq.answer: Troggs invaded from below, and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque tried to destroy them by opening the city's radioactive waste tanks on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's advice. The plan was meant to flood only the lower sectors, but deadly radiation seeped throughout Gnomeregan, killing eighty percent of the gnomish population and mutating survivors.

faq.q: Where did all the troggs come from?
aliases: why are there troggs in gnomeregan
faq.answer: The troggs were ancient creatures roused from deep subterranean slumber by dwarven archaeological excavations at Uldaman, a titan complex. Drawn to the heat and vibrations of Gnomeregan's heavy machinery, they dug extensive tunnels into the city's lower levels and engineering quarters.

faq.q: Why didn't the gnomes ask the Alliance for help against the troggs?
faq.answer: The trogg invasion struck during the Third War, as the Scourge brought down the Kingdom of Lordaeron, and the gnomes fought with their own technology and soldiers. No record explains why High Tinker Mekkatorque never called for outside aid; he turned instead to venting the city's radioactive waste tanks.

aliases: why are the gnomes green and crazy
faq.answer: Leper gnomes are survivors of Gnomeregan's radioactive venting, left with severe physical and mental corruption from prolonged exposure. Their skin turned sickly pale green, their bodies became blistered and diseased, and their minds decayed into raving, homicidal mania under Mekgineer Thermaplugg's thrall.

Mekgineer Thermaplugg was High Tinker Mekkatorque's trusted chief advisor, though he secretly coveted the High Tinker office. At his urging, the city was flooded with radiation, and Mekkatorque calls him the betrayer of the gnomish people. Irradiated along with the city, Thermaplugg rules as a deranged leper despot from Tinkers' Court.

faq.q: What changes after Mekgineer Thermaplugg is defeated?
faq.answer: Defeating Thermaplugg cuts off the leadership directing the leper gnomes and rogue defenses. Lethal radiation and thick trogg infestations still choke the lower corridors, so Mekkatorque must prepare deeper excavations before the city can be fully reclaimed.

faq.q: Why are the Dark Iron dwarves inside Gnomeregan?
aliases: why are dark irons in gnomeregan
faq.answer: The Dark Iron clan sent emissaries into Gnomeregan, represented by the Dark Iron Ambassador. Eager to sabotage Ironforge and the Alliance, the Dark Irons seek an alliance with Thermaplugg and hope to use gnomish technology and weaponized machinery in their own war efforts.

faq.q: Where are the surviving gnomes living now?
faq.answer: After the radioactive catastrophe, the surviving untainted gnomes fled through the mountains to Ironforge. Their dwarven cousins gave them sanctuary in Tinkertown, an engineering enclave within the mountain fortress. There Gelbin Mekkatorque governs his exiled people and plans their eventual homecoming.

angles.text: As a gnome, Gnomeregan holds your people's deepest tragedy and enduring shame. Entering its halls is a harrowing pilgrimage to avenge eighty percent of your fallen race and dethrone the traitor Thermaplugg.

As a dwarf, your kinship with the gnomes reaches back to the ancestors who helped lay Gnomeregan's foundations. Dwarven excavations at Uldaman also unwittingly unleashed the trogg hordes that ruined it.
As an Alliance member, you stand with a people who fought beside the Alliance in the Second War. Liberating Gnomeregan from Thermaplugg is vital to restoring gnomish strength within the faction.
As an engineer, you can find advanced masterworks, schematics, and experimental contraptions in Gnomeregan's ruins. Its blueprints remain invaluable amid lethal mechanical chaos.
